description: Cyber Islamic Resistance is a pro‑Iranian hacktivist collective that blends public acts of defacement, DDoS and hack‑and‑leak campaigns with sophisticated infiltration of critical infrastructure and OT/ICS environments. Their operations span government, finance and energy sectors across multiple regions, employing a mix of phishing, custom malware, WebShells and emerging C2 channels such as Ethereum smart contracts and satellite backbones.
goals: CIR’s strategic objectives revolve around geopolitical propaganda, disruption and retaliation in the context of the Iran–Israel conflict, while simultaneously projecting adversarial influence over Western institutions. It focuses on sectors that have broad societal impact—energy, water utilities, finance, healthcare—and leverages both cyber‑defacement to generate public notoriety and covert attacks aimed at disabling or exfiltrating sensitive data. Their targeting strategy includes mass phishing campaigns against government employees, credential spraying techniques (OWA, SMTP), and an active pursuit of vulnerabilities in OT/ICS stacks to extend operational scope.
